memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses gave an order and they sent this word throughout the camp: 'No man or woman is to make anything else as an offering for the sanctuary.' And so the people were restrained from bringing more, because what they already had was more than enough to do all the work." - Exod 36:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A public announcement went out through the camp telling people to stop giving. Moses had to restrain them.

There is something almost humorous in it, and something deeply challenging. Most of us have never been in a church where the message was "please stop."

But look closer, because there is wisdom here beyond the generosity. Moses knew when enough was enough. He did not accept more simply because it was offered, and he did not build a bigger project just because resources kept arriving. God had given a design, and the design defined the need.

That is worth learning. Growth is not always faithfulness. Sometimes the godly decision is to say, "we have what God asked for; we will not expand beyond it."

Notice too the integrity on display. Moses handled other people's offerings with complete transparency. Paul took similar care with money entrusted to him, wanting to do what is right not only in the eyes of the Lord but also in the eyes of man (2 Cor 8:21).

God's work never lacks when God's people are willing. And leaders who fear God know when to stop asking.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you know when you have enough, or does more always feel necessary?
2. Are you handling what others entrust to you with full integrity?
3. Where might God be saying "this is enough" to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me contentment to know when enough is enough, and integrity in everything entrusted to me. Amen.
